newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Luxembourg EU presidency starts in earnest.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg EU presidency starts in earnest.

text.p: Luxembourg's turn at the helm of the European Union kicked off in earnest on Thursday with an official visit from the European Commission for talks on coordinating the work of the next six months.
After discussions with individual ministers in the morning, the commissioners joined Luxembourg's Grand Duke Jean for lunch. A news conference will follow a plenary session in the afternoon.

The main formal goal during Luxembourg's six-month stint in the hot seat is preparing the EU for eastward expansion, but it will also have to ensure plans for a single European currency, the Euro, remain firmly on track.

"It will be a continuing discussion whether the Euro comes on time and with which countries. (The debate) will not leave us for a day," Foreign Minister Jacques Poos told reporters at an informal meeting late on Wednesday.

Membership talks with central and eastern European countries wanting to join the wealthy western club are due to start six months after the agreement of a new EU treaty, which was reached on June 17 at a summit in Amsterdam.

On July 16 the European Commission is due to publish its recommendations on their readiness to join, and the presidency has the delicate task of working out the method by which the enlargement talks will proceed, and with how many countries.

With increasing demands for Europe to do more to fight unemployment, Luxembourg has also been given the job of holding a summit on jobs in the autumn, with November 22 now pencilled in as a possible date.

Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker has already sent a letter this week to his European counterparts asking them to suggest experiences of fighting unemployment which have proved successful in their countries.
Replies were expected by the end of July, a Luxembourg official said.
